items.title: Hackers repeatedly breached suppliers holding UK police data, watchdog finds

items.title: University of New Mexico hospital diverts ambulances after cyberattack
items.snippet: For about two hours on Monday, the organization diverted ambulances to health systems in Albuquerque and Santa Fe. They were forced to suspend outpatient surgeries and appointments for the remainder of the day.
items.summary: The University of New Mexico hospital diverted ambulances for about two hours after a cyberattack and suspended outpatient surgeries and appointments for the rest of the day.
items.why: Check that incident plans cover ambulance diversions and continuity of clinical services.

items.title: Tailscale warns of SSH flaws allowing root privilege escalation

items.title: Malicious apps prey on Russians’ anxiety about fuel prices, drone strikes

items.title: Moscow faces internet disruptions as foreign leaders gather for summits

items.title: How the Pentagon wants to buy cyber outcomes, not equipment

items.title: USAF should buy newly designed air refuelers to meet China threat: Report

learn.explainer: Telemetry is data collected and transmitted about a system’s activity or condition. Here, the Warp report says user telemetry was exposed.
CASEVAC means casualty evacuation: moving wounded people away from a battlefield or other dangerous area. The StarGate report describes an aerial platform for this purpose.
Acute hunger refers to a serious, immediate lack of food. The Sudan report links the risk to conflict, drought and funding cuts.

analysis.headline: Capability, exposure and choices across the briefing
paragraphs: Today’s top stories span diplomatic participation, defense procurement, navigation systems and battlefield evacuation, alongside cybersecurity exposures. Together they show how institutions weigh participation and investment while technologies and data remain part of operational decisions. The snippets offer limited detail, so connections between these issues should be treated cautiously.

The cyber advisories name vulnerabilities in industrial products, while Warp’s report concerns exposed agent logs and telemetry after an attack on a third-party vendor. These are distinct forms of risk; together, they suggest defenders should track both deployed systems and supplier access. The advisory snippets do not specify full impacts.

The drone report describes claimed evacuations, including a mission under electronic attack; the navigation-platform item highlights an INS and GNSS receiver. Their operational relevance may warrant attention, but the snippets do not establish performance beyond what they state. Analysts can watch how procurement, cooperation and participation choices develop.
takeaways: Check affected industrial products against the complete CISA advisories.
Review third-party access to sensitive logs and telemetry.
Treat reported operational capabilities as claims, not independently established outcomes.
